materials.title: Drops Stayed on the Outside
materials.text:
A textile display compared a treated cloth with an untreated sample. Water formed ____1____ on one surface, small rounded drops rather than a continuous sheet. On the other sample, the liquid could ____2____, covering a wider surface area. The tutor treated the observed shapes as part of a wetting relationship, not as a complete test of every garment property.

The contact ____3____ described the geometry where the liquid boundary met the solid under the stated convention. Surface ____4____ concerned the texture of the material at the relevant scale. Both the surface chemistry and its structure could matter to the behaviour shown.

A water-avoiding surface was called ____5____ in the explanation. A ____6____ added to the cloth could alter that surface. The demonstration did not assume that a treatment changed every part of the underlying fabric into the same material.

The cloth’s ____7____ were the elongated elements making its structure. Spaces or openings within the material were ____8____. A material described as ____9____ allowed the relevant substance to pass through under specified conditions; one that made visible drops form outside was not automatically impermeable under every pressure or duration.

The sample could also ____10____ some water, taking it into the material rather than only carrying it as an external drop. The class kept absorption, surface wetting and passage through the cloth separate. A full garment additionally had joins and use conditions. The display therefore resisted a universal claim from one attractive photograph of beaded water and explained exactly which interaction had been observed.

materials.title: A Model Key Met a Model Lock
materials.text:
A museum used a transparent toy mechanism to explain why matching parts matter. The outer ____1____ held the moving components. Within it, a ____2____ was the round part designed to turn under the displayed arrangement. The model contained no actual security device visitors could operate elsewhere.

The ____3____ was the opening shaped to accept the corresponding toy key. The key’s ____4____ described its cross-sectional shape, not merely the pattern along one edge. A matching outline allowed entry into the displayed opening but did not by itself establish every internal condition needed for movement.

Long ____5____ ran along the key in the model. A particular edge feature was a ____6____, a shaped indentation made as part of the intended design. The tutor separated those features rather than calling every mark a number printed on the metal.

The moving pieces called ____7____ responded to the inserted model key. The displayed ____8____ supplied a restoring force to one part. When the relevant pieces were ____9____ under the toy’s stated rule, the central component could ____10____. The demonstration connected these named relationships without supplying dimensions, decoding methods or techniques for opening a real lock.

The lesson’s point was structural: an object could fit through an opening while still failing to meet the conditions for the intended action. The model provided all relevant labels and behaviour in the text. No hidden diagram was required, and the example did not imply that all real lock designs used the same components or responded to the same arrangement.

materials.title: The Note Changed as the Source Passed
materials.text:
A recorded classroom demonstration compared a sound source moving past a listener with one remaining still. The source ____1____ a repeating disturbance, sending it into the surrounding air. The air was the ____2____ through which that disturbance travelled in the simplified account.

A source described as ____3____ moved towards the listener. Ahead of it, successive wave fronts were closer together, or ____4____, under the stated conditions. The ____5____ was the distance between corresponding successive parts of the wave. It differed from the physical size of the source itself.

At the listener, ____6____ described the number of wave cycles arriving per unit time. The perceived ____7____ related to how high or low the note sounded, not simply how loud it was. The tutor kept these concepts connected but did not treat a perceptual description as identical to every physical measurement.

When the source was ____8____, it moved away instead. The relationship between emitted and received patterns could differ across that change. The ____9____ effect named this shift associated with motion between the relevant source, listener and medium conditions. The lesson did not claim that the device had necessarily switched to another note inside its mechanism.

The analysis depended on ____10____ motion, movement considered between specified objects rather than an unexplained label moving. Loudness could change too, but it was not a substitute for explaining the changed spacing and arrival rate. The recorded example supplied all evidence and required neither a live sound exposure nor observation beside actual traffic.

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: sent disturbance defines emitted发出。compressed受压状态非主动发声事件，stationary形容静止不谓发送。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: air sound travels through defines medium介质。volume体积或响度非传播物质，crest波峰形状异。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: towards listener defines approaching靠近。receding远离下空相反，stationary相对静不向近。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: fronts closer spacing defines compressed压缩的。emitted发出不表间隔变近，stationary静不压缩。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: distance repeating wave parts defines wavelength波长。amplitude振幅是偏离幅量，speed速率非波周期空间长。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: cycles arrive per time defines frequency频率。volume响度、speed传播速非每时周期数。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: perceived high low defines pitch音高。volume感响大小与此区别，amplitude物理振幅非音高感。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: away source defines receding远离。approaching向近相反，stationary静止不是离开。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: motion-linked received shift defines Doppler多普勒。其他候选不命名此具名效应，pitch为结果感受不是效应专名。

questions.prompt: The Note Changed as the Source Passed: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: between specified objects motion defines relative相对的。stationary静止可能仅一参照状态，speed名词不修运动关系。

materials.title: The Leaf Opened Its Pores at Night
materials.text:
A greenhouse class studied one plant using the particular carbon-processing pattern described in its display. Its thick tissues were ____1____, fleshy and able to hold substantial water. This was an ____2____ associated with the conditions considered, a feature contributing to the organism’s functioning rather than a conscious decision made by the individual during the lesson.

The habitat described as ____3____ had little available moisture. Water loss through the plant’s gas-exchange structures mattered in that setting. Those small openings were ____4____. The tutor distinguished the opening itself from the larger tissues in which it occurred.

In the displayed pattern, much of the initial gas intake happened at ____5____, during the dark period. Incoming ____6____ was incorporated into an organic ____7____ for temporary retention. The account described one physiological arrangement rather than claiming that every plant used identical timing.

During ____8____, when light was available, the retained material could contribute to ____9____ under the stated process. Opening the gas-exchange structures widely at the same time was not required in the same way as in the contrasting example. The tutor separated the timing of the initial intake from every light-dependent part of the later activity.

____10____ referred to the loss of water vapour from the plant in this context. The class did not interpret lower loss as proof that the plant could live without water or that light had become unnecessary. The example showed a coordination of structure and timing under a particular environment. It supplied concepts for interpreting the described plant, not a universal care schedule for every cactus or succulent.

questions.prompt: The Leaf Opened Its Pores at Night: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.

materials.title: The Same Lines, Folded Another Way
materials.text:
A paper-folding class began with a ____1____, a sheet whose four sides were equal and adjacent sides met at right angles. Its outer ____2____ was a boundary line, while a ____3____ was a corner where relevant lines met. The tutor distinguished these parts before asking learners to follow a printed plan.

A fold left a ____4____, a line in the paper marking where it had bent. A ____5____ connected opposite corners. The class did not assume that every printed line asked the learner to cut through the sheet.

Under the diagram’s convention, a ____6____ fold rose like a ridge when viewed from the stated side. A ____7____ fold formed a trough from that same viewpoint. Changing which side was viewed could change the description, so the plan’s ____8____ had to remain clear. The tutor kept the reference view with the instructions rather than allowing the words to float free of it.

The ____9____ of operations mattered. Several final crease lines did not uniquely determine how the model had been assembled or which layer should move first. An apparently identical set of marks could support more than one possible folding history.

The model’s ____10____ concerned the correspondence of parts across its stated reflection line. It was not guaranteed merely because the original sheet had four equal sides. The class compared the finished arrangement with the intended plan and preserved which side and stage each instruction described. The lesson made the geometry and process explicit without requiring learners to infer a missing diagram from a few unexplained arrows.

questions.explanation: four equal sides right angles defines square正方形。layer纸层非形状，flat平不保证四等边直角。

questions.prompt: The Same Lines, Folded Another Way: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: outer boundary defines edge边。crease内折痕不必外缘，vertex角点非边线。

questions.prompt: The Same Lines, Folded Another Way: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.

questions.explanation: connect opposite corners defines diagonal对角线。perpendicular相互直角形容性非跨角线名，edge邻角边不同。

questions.prompt: The Same Lines, Folded Another Way: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: rises ridge given side defines mountain山折。valley谷折相反，layer层非折向。

questions.prompt: The Same Lines, Folded Another Way: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: trough given side defines valley谷折。mountain隆起相反，reversible可逆非凹向名称。

materials.title: A New Piece in an Old Mosaic
materials.text:
An art workshop studied a fictional mosaic panel and a labelled reconstruction. Its small individual pieces were ____1____ under the technical term supplied by the tutor. The supporting layer behind the design was its ____2____. The picture depended on the arrangement of separate pieces as well as on their individual colours.

A full-size preparatory drawing was called a ____3____ in this art context. The design could be ____4____ onto another surface, following its lines to transfer their arrangement. The familiar word for a humorous drawing therefore had another specialised role in the workshop.

The pieces were placed during ____5____, the stage when their intended positions were established in the supporting material. Spaces between them were ____6____. The material filling those joints was ____7____ in the account. The tutor distinguished the joint-filling role from every material used behind or beneath the pieces.

A replacement piece was marked separately from ____8____ material retained from the earlier panel. A close visual match did not make a newly supplied part historically old. The record kept what had been retained and what had been added available for later checking.

The surface’s ____9____ concerned its felt or visible roughness and relief rather than its colour alone. The overall aim of ____10____ was to care for the object and its relevant evidence under the exercise’s stated approach. It was not a demand to make every old work look newly manufactured. The labelled example supplied the history needed for discussion and did not authorise treatment of an actual historic panel.

materials.title: The Contract Could Not See Every Action
materials.text:
A fictional economics tutorial examined a person hiring another to carry out a task. The party delegating the work was the ____1____. The party acting on that delegation was the ____2____. The model did not assume that their interests were automatically identical simply because an agreement existed.

The hired party chose ____3____, the costly action devoted to the task. Some of that action was ____4____ to the employer under the stipulated conditions: it could not be directly seen in the required way. The final ____5____ depended on that action and other influences, so a disappointing result did not uniquely reveal what the worker had done.

An ____6____ affected the relative attractiveness of choices. A payment rule could encourage one action rather than another without guaranteeing a perfect response. The tutorial examined those trade-offs rather than describing every reward as a universal solution to coordination.

A ____7____ provided information related to hidden action or type under the model. It was not automatically a direct, error-free measurement of every relevant quality. Checking activity through ____8____ could supply further information while also requiring resources and an account of what the check actually revealed.

The class distinguished information that one party could observe from information that was ____9____ to the institution charged with enforcing the agreement. A private observation did not automatically become a fact that a third party could establish under the rules. A condition suitable for inclusion and enforcement was ____10____ under the exercise’s definition.

The lesson also separated uncertainty about action after agreement from uncertainty about a party’s earlier characteristics. Those were different information problems and could call for different arrangements. The final analysis connected the delegated task, information and incentives rather than treating a well-written payment sentence as proof that all interests had become perfectly aligned.

questions.explanation: final result action plus others defines outcome结果。signal信息信号可有关但不等任务最终后果，risk泛风险非具体实现。

questions.prompt: The Contract Could Not See Every Action: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: relative choice attractiveness defines incentive激励。alignment利益一致是可能目标非改变选择报酬机制名。

questions.prompt: The Contract Could Not See Every Action: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.

questions.prompt: The Contract Could Not See Every Action: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: checking activity defines monitoring监督。selection挑选人非履约中检查，risk风险非查核活动。

questions.explanation: condition enforceable agreement defines contractible可写入执行合同的。verifiable可证是条件非整体可入约概念，adverse不利不表法律可约。

materials.title: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission
materials.text:
A fictional epidemiology seminar examined a model of spread in a defined population. Its ____1____ number described the average number of new infections generated by one infected person under the stated conditions. The resulting infections were ____2____ to that source in the model’s account, not an estimate that every person would transmit to exactly the same number.

People able to acquire the infection under the model were ____3____. A person capable of passing it on during a stated period was ____4____. Those descriptions concerned different roles and could not be replaced by one broad label meaning affected in some way.

The ____5____ number reflected the current conditions rather than the idealised fully susceptible setting used for another defined measure. Behaviour, immunity and control arrangements could therefore affect its value. The class retained those assumptions instead of treating the number as an unchanging property printed on the pathogen.

An ____6____ altered the conditions relevant to spread. The comparison required an account of what would happen without that change, not merely the observation that a measure had been announced before a later trend.

____7____ counted new infections or defined events occurring within a stated interval. ____8____ concerned the existing proportion or number affected at a time under the chosen definition. These measures answered different questions even when their names appeared together in a report.

The ____9____ interval concerned the timing between infection of a source and infection of a person it infected. A given reproduction value could correspond to different speeds of growth when that timing differed. Finally, ____10____ described how unevenly onward transmission was distributed. A mean alone did not reveal that heterogeneity. The lesson offered no forecast or medical advice; it explained why population, timing and variation remained part of interpreting the supplied model.

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: average onward infections reproduction number再生数。generation间隔说时间非每人继发数，threshold界限不是传播平均名。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: new infections linked initial source defines secondary继发的。variant变异株名非来源后代事件位置，universal普遍不表继发。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: able acquire infection defines susceptible易感的。infectious可传给人下一空相反角色，effective有效不指可被感染状态。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: capable passing defines infectious有传染性的。susceptible易感可未感染传染，secondary继发不保证当下能传。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: current conditions reproduction defines effective有效的。universal通用不保条件，threshold阈值不是当前条件修饰词。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: alter spread conditions defines intervention干预。delay迟滞时间不是主动改变措施，variant变体可改变但非此措施概念。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: new events interval defines incidence发病/新发量。prevalence现有量下空，cases个例总称不特指每期新发生测量。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: existing affected at time defines prevalence患病量/率。incidence新发生非存量，delay时间量不同。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: source infection to recipient infection defines generation代际间隔。delay泛时间差不专此流行病传播定义，other不合。

questions.prompt: One Average Did Not Describe Every Transmission: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: uneven transmission distribution defines dispersion离散度。reproduction均值非异质性，threshold越界值不表分散程度。

materials.title: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links
materials.text:
A fictional mathematics class represented workers and tasks in a graph. Workers formed one set and tasks another. Links connected a worker only with a task, not with another worker in the same set. This made the graph ____1____. Its entities were ____2____, and the allowed worker–task relationships were ____3____.

A ____4____ selected links so no worker or task was used more than once in the stated arrangement. The number of selected links was its ____5____. The class kept a set of possible relationships separate from an actual compatible selection among them.

A ____6____ matching had the largest possible number of selected links in the graph. It did not necessarily use every entity. A ____7____ matching covered all entities under the exercise’s definition. These requirements were not interchangeable: the best available selection could still leave someone or something unmatched.

For the feasibility question studied, the team examined each ____8____ of workers, a selected group from that side. Its ____9____ were the tasks connected to at least one worker in the group. Having enough tasks in total did not guarantee enough suitable tasks for every such group. A concentrated shortage of relationships could obstruct the desired assignment even when the headline counts looked sufficient.

An ____10____ path alternated between selected and unselected links in the way specified by the method, allowing a compatible change that increased the selected count. The tutor distinguished that operation from simply adding an arbitrary link and hoping no conflict appeared.

The exercise showed why counting opportunities and constructing a valid assignment were different tasks. It supplied all relationships in words and asserted no actual employment allocation. A graph could expose a structural limit, while the choice of which real-world constraints it represented remained a separate modelling decision.

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: two sets cross links only defines bipartite二分的。weighted加权另属性，adjacent相邻不命名两部图类。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: entities graph defines nodes节点。edges关系下空，subset组而非通用实体单元名。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: allowed cross relationships defines edges边。neighbours邻接实体集合不是连接关系本身。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: links no shared worker/task defines matching匹配。cover覆盖未必每点至多一次，subset任意子集未保兼容。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: selected links count defines cardinality基数。maximum最大性质非数量测度名，cover覆盖集合不等元素数。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: largest count defines maximum最大。perfect每实体全覆下空更强，saturated饱和对实体状态不表全图最大规模。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: covers every entity defines perfect完美。maximum全图最好未必全覆，feasible仅可行未必完整。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: selected group from worker set defines subset子集。matching选边而非取工人组，cover覆盖对象非单纯任何一组。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: tasks connected group defines neighbours邻集。nodes泛全部点未限邻接，edges是线不是邻接任务实体。

questions.prompt: Enough Tasks, but Not Enough Suitable Links: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: alternating path increases selection defines augmenting增广的。adjacent只相邻不保可增长交替路，weighted权重不是增匹配结构。

materials.title: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission
materials.text:
A fictional textual-scholarship workshop compared several copies of an old work. Each surviving ____1____ supplied evidence for a textual state, not direct access to the author’s final intention. Systematic ____2____ aligned corresponding locations to identify agreements and differences. The class did not judge a copy merely by how neatly its script had been written.

A ____3____ was the form of wording found or proposed at a specified location. A shortened written form was an ____4____ in the comparison. Neither label alone established which was earlier or preferable. The account required reasons linking the local evidence with the question being asked.

The ____5____ was the person who produced a copy. The source copy used for that work was its ____6____. A present-day collection location did not automatically identify that source or the route of transmission.

A ____7____ was a gap in the text, such as the omission shared by two manuscripts in the example. A shared error could support a relationship, but the class considered whether it could have arisen independently. Resemblance did not make a particular history inevitable without further evidence.

A ____8____ represented the proposed relationships among copies as a branching diagram. The inferred ____9____ was a common ancestor within that proposed account, not necessarily the author’s original manuscript. The notation therefore kept a reconstructed ancestral state distinct from a physically surviving object.

The model also allowed ____10____, the mixing of textual material from more than one source line. That possibility complicated a strictly branching representation. The final account treated the diagram as an argued historical hypothesis rather than a picture guaranteed by a software command. The manuscripts were invented for the exercise, so the lesson made no claim about an actual literary work or the pedigree of a real archive.

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: surviving copy evidence textual state defines witness见证本。exemplar抄写所据本不必现存见证，每副本证据角色更广。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: systematic alignment differences defines collation校勘比对。recension修订文本形态不是逐点比较动作，emendation改订不同。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: wording at location defines reading读法。abbreviation特指缩写类别下一空，vernacular本地语言不指一处文字形式。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: shortened written form且an前定义abbreviation缩写。reading任何局部读法不特指缩短类别，wrinkles皱纹非文字缩写。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: person makes copy defines copyist抄写员。witness证据本非人，archetype祖本状态非制作者。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: source copy for copying defines exemplar底本。archetype推共同祖不必某抄手直接底本，stemma关系图不是书本。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: gap omission defines lacuna缺文。emendation编辑补改动作非原文空缺，variant不同形式不必缺失。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: branching copy relationships diagram defines stemma谱系图。recension文本修订形态非树状关系图，archetype树祖点不是全图。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: inferred common ancestor defines archetype祖本。exemplar直接所据本不等全支共同祖，independent形容独立不作祖态名。

questions.prompt: Two Copies Shared the Same Omission: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: material mixed multiple transmission sources defines contamination混合传承。collation比较不引混来源，emendation编辑改可无第二支来源。

materials.title: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages
materials.text:
A fictional hydrogeology seminar examined water collected from a well. The ____1____ represented a limited amount taken under a stated procedure. It did not automatically preserve a separate labelled history for every molecule that had arrived from different parts of the aquifer.

____2____ named water entering the groundwater system from the relevant input under the account. A ____3____ was a substance whose measured behaviour supplied information about movement or history. The tutor stated how that substance entered and behaved instead of treating any detected chemical as a clock that ran under identical conditions everywhere.

The elapsed ____4____ since the relevant entry event was a quantity the team sought to interpret. A measured concentration could reflect ____5____ of water with different histories rather than one single journey. The resulting age ____6____ described a range of contributions and their weights, not a promise that every part of the sample shared one number.

Transport carried with the bulk water movement was ____7____. Spreading related to different flow paths and local conditions was ____8____ under the model. A chemical that interacted with the solid material could also experience ____9____, delayed movement relative to the water. These mechanisms affected how a measured substance related to the water whose history it was intended to reveal.

For a radioactive tracer, the ____10____ was the time associated with reduction to half through the stated decay process. That parameter did not eliminate the need to understand input history, mixing or other relevant changes. The exercise supplied a method of interpreting a signal rather than a direct date stamp on every molecule. Its conclusions remained conditional on the tracer model and the sample’s relationship to the flow system; no actual well was dated.

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: limited collected amount defines sample样品。porosity介质空隙量非取来的水份，distribution分布抽象非一瓶样。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: water enters groundwater system defines recharge补给。reversed逆向形容词、sediment沉积物不是水进入过程。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: substance informative movement history defines tracer示踪剂。velocity水速物理量非化学追踪物，age历时不是物质。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: elapsed since defined entry defines age年龄。sediment沉积物、velocity速度不指进入以来历时，other不合。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: combining distinct histories defines mixing混合。dispersion传播展宽机制下文，不等取样中多来源贡献合并的一般过程。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: range ages weights defines distribution分布。uniform均匀形容词不名加权范围，porosity空隙率非年龄谱。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: bulk fluid transport defines advection平流。dispersion差路径扩展下空，retardation相对水延迟非随水带。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: spread differing flow routes defines dispersion弥散。advection整体携带不同，mixing可结果但不是模型传播展宽专称。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: chemical delay solid interaction defines retardation滞留。sediment沉积物可能参与作用却不是相对水移动延迟过程名，velocity速度量非延迟作用。

questions.prompt: A Sample Contained Water of Different Ages: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: time decay half defines half-life半衰期。age样品历时不是核素减半固有参数，velocity速度不是减半衰变历时。

materials.title: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?
materials.text:
A fictional security seminar considered a document distributed with a digital ____1____, a cryptographic value linked to the message and the signing process. This was not a scanned picture of a handwritten name. Its role depended on specified algorithms, keys and the assumptions of the system.

The signer’s ____2____ key was kept secret under that arrangement. The corresponding ____3____ key could be used by others for the relevant check. Giving those roles different labels did not make an implementation secure by itself; the handling and trust arrangements still mattered.

A ____4____ function mapped the document into a fixed-format summary under its stated design. A ____5____ would occur if two different inputs produced the same summary value under that function. The seminar explained the resistance properties needed by the scheme rather than claiming that any short checksum supplied the same security.

____6____ tested the signature against the message and the relevant key under the specified procedure. A successful result contributed evidence about ____7____, whether the signed content had been altered in the relevant way. It did not establish that every factual statement inside that content was true.

A ____8____ linked a key with an asserted identity under an issuer’s arrangements. The team examined why the issuer should be relied on and whether the relationship still applied. A later ____9____ could withdraw the status of a credential under the system’s process. A familiar name in a file was not a substitute for that account.

Finally, ____10____ concerned keeping content from unauthorised readers. Signing alone did not guarantee it: a message could be publicly readable while carrying a valid signature. The exercise distinguished integrity, identity claims and secrecy, showing why one successful cryptographic check could answer an important question without answering every other question about the document or its author.

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 1.
questions.explanation: message-linked cryptographic signing value defines signature签名。timestamp时间凭据非签消息数值总称，certificate身份绑定不同。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 2.
questions.explanation: signer secret key defines private私钥的。public公开检查下空相反，trusted可信关系不定义保密密钥类型。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 3.
questions.explanation: counterpart others check defines public公钥的。private秘密一方相反，forged伪造不是合法检查密钥类。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 4.
questions.explanation: function fixed summary defines hash哈希。collision是不同输入同输出的事件下空，非摘要映射函数，encryption加密不是摘要映射。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 5.
questions.explanation: different inputs same summary defines collision碰撞。hash指函数不指这事件，signature带签名密钥运算不命名摘要重合现象。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 6.
questions.explanation: signature checked message key defines verification验证。encryption加密隐藏内容而非检验签名，不表此核验操作。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 7.
questions.explanation: signed content unaltered defines integrity完整性。confidentiality秘密最后空相反，identity是谁而非内容未变。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 8.
questions.explanation: issuer key identity binding defines certificate证书。timestamp绑定时刻非密钥身份文书，signature密码值不独定义issuer关系。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 9.
questions.explanation: withdraw credential status defines revocation撤销。verification检验状态非作废，forged形容伪造不名流程。

questions.prompt: The Signature Verified, but Was the Claim True?: choose the unchanged word for gap 10.
questions.explanation: prevent unauthorised reading defines confidentiality机密性。integrity防改非防读，identity身份不是内容保密。
